record.paper_title: Vector bundles on curves and generalized theta functions: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let U*_X(k) be the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on a compact Riemann surface X of rank k and degree k(g−1), let M = O(Θ_k) be its canonical theta line bundle, and let ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) → H^0(U*_X(k), M^r)^* be the linear map induced by the divisor τ_{k,r}^*Θ_{kr} under tensor product. Is ϑ_{k,r} always an isomorphism?

evidence.quote: Let me denote by U*_X(k) the moduli space of semi-stable vector bundles of rank k and degree k(g − 1) on X ; it is isomorphic (non canonically) to U_X(k) .
we get a linear map ϑ_{k,r} : H0(SU_X(r), L^k) −→ H0(U*_X(k), M^r)^* , well-defined up to a scalar.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. For positive integers $r$ and $k$, let $\mathcal{SU}_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on $X$ of rank $r$ and trivial determinant, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be its ample generator (the determinant line bundle), so that $H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k)$ is the space of rank-$r$, level-$k$ generalized theta functions.

Let $\mathcal{U}^*_X(k)$ denote the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on $X$ of rank $k$ and degree $k(g-1)$. On $\mathcal{U}^*_X(k)$ there is a canonical theta divisor: for a generic $E \in \mathcal{U}^*_X(k)$, the locus
$$\Theta_k = \{E \in \mathcal{U}^*_X(k) \mid h^0(X,E) \neq 0\}$$
is a divisor; let $\mathcal{M} = \mathcal{O}(\Theta_k)$ be the associated line bundle.

Consider the tensor product map
$$\tau_{k,r}: \mathcal{SU}_X(r) \times \mathcal{U}^*_X(k) \longrightarrow \mathcal{U}^*_X(kr), \qquad (F,E) \mapsto F \otimes E,$$
and note that $\tau_{k,r}^* \mathcal{O}(\Theta_{kr}) = \mathcal{L}^k \boxtimes \mathcal{M}^r$. The locus
$$D_{k,r} = \{(F,E) \mid h^0(X, F \otimes E) \neq 0\} \subset \mathcal{SU}_X(r) \times \mathcal{U}^*_X(k)$$
is (when nonempty as a divisor) a divisor in the linear system $|\mathcal{L}^k \boxtimes \mathcal{M}^r|$, and so determines a section, hence (up to scalar) a linear map
$$\vartheta_{k,r}: H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k) \longrightarrow H^0(\mathcal{U}^*_X(k), \mathcal{M}^r)^*.$$

The two spaces in question are known to have the same dimension. Prove or disprove: for every compact Riemann surface $X$ of genus $g \geq 2$ and all positive integers $k, r$, the map $\vartheta_{k,r}$ is an isomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: The strange duality conjecture (Beauville–Donagi–Tu) was proved for generic curves by P. Belkale (2006), and subsequently for all smooth curves by A. Marian and D. Oprea. Belkale later established flatness of the strange duality map over the moduli of curves, completing the picture. The conjecture as stated is therefore solved.

status_evidence.title: The strange duality conjecture for generic curves
status_evidence.snippet: Belkale proves the strange duality conjecture for a generic smooth projective curve.
status_evidence.claim: Strange duality holds for generic curves.

status_evidence.title: The rank-level duality for non-abelian theta functions (Marian–Oprea)
status_evidence.snippet: Marian and Oprea prove the strange duality conjecture of Beauville–Donagi–Tu holds for all curves.
status_evidence.claim: Strange duality holds for all smooth curves.

status_evidence.title: La dualité étrange [d'après P. Belkale, A. Marian et D. Oprea]
status_evidence.snippet: Bourbaki seminar exposition of the proof of strange duality by Belkale and by Marian–Oprea.
